solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's quite untrue such a novel wouldn't corrupt

definitions.meaning: something completely made up and invented is quite untrue
a novel that is clean, morally unsullied storytelling would corrupt nobody

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a claim as false, then muses on a wholesome novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an outright fabrication, and literally a chaste or wholesome work of invented storytelling.

clue.text: Sort of holiday for which you need to get cases ready on time

parts.note: to pack is to fill suitcases before a trip
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Advice for travellers: be packed and punctual for your trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A package holiday is an all-inclusive tour sold as one deal, so the word names a sort of holiday.

clue.text: Two kings embracing are not seen so often

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the pair of letters wraps around the word inside

parts.note: R (Rex) is the abbreviation for king, so two kings give two Rs

explanation.surface: A pair of monarchs hugging is an unusual sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative adjective: what is seen less often is more uncommon, scarcer.

clue.text: Not a scrap of bias

parts.note: reads as 'no trace of prejudice at all', but a scrap is also a brawl, so a scrap with no bias is an even contest

explanation.surface: A claim of total impartiality.
explanation.definitionFit: An even, honest contest between equals is a scrap with no bias in it.

clue.text: Accountants pocketing hundreds? The scoundrels!

indicators.note: to pocket is to take something inside, so these letters hold the other piece

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, here standing for hundreds

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at accountants embezzling large sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cads are dishonourable men, rotters or scoundrels.

clue.text: Blameless cleric who had trouble with King John

definitions.text: cleric who had trouble with King John
definitions.meaning: Pope ... III placed England under interdict and excommunicated King John during their dispute over the Archbishop of Canterbury

explanation.surface: A history note about a churchman in conflict with an English king.
explanation.walkthrough: King John ruled England 1199-1216; his quarrel with the Pope ended with England briefly a papal fief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: guiltless, and the name of Pope Innocent III, King John's adversary.

clue.text: Nearly time — time for bed

parts.note: nigh means near or nearly

explanation.surface: A reminder that bedtime is approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are when people go to bed, so this is a fair descriptive definition.

clue.text: Struggle to study with care

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
to tend is to look after or care for

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to study carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to contend is to strive or struggle against difficulties or opponents.

clue.text: Frightened from the beginning then went ahead

parts.note: a start is a beginning
led means went in front, at the head

explanation.surface: Someone was scared from the outset yet pressed on in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: startled means given a sudden fright or shock.

clue.text: Girl and chap at university flirted

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
a don is a university lecturer or fellow

explanation.surface: Gossip that a young woman and an academic had a fling.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to carry on with someone is to have a flirtation or affair.

clue.text: Boarded, and did well with studies?

definitions.meaning: got onto a bus, train or ship
made progress or succeeded, as a pupil does in lessons

explanation.surface: A question about whether a boarding-school pupil made good progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: climbed aboard a vehicle, and prospered or advanced in work.

clue.text: Undirected commercial break

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A TV advertising interval that wanders aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting without steering is undirected, floating loose with no course.

clue.text: Clear of secret corruption

indicators.note: corruption means spoiling or distortion, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is cleared of a hidden scandal of graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is fodder as well as 'secret': the eight letters OF SECRET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to get off scot-free is to escape clear, without penalty.

clue.text: Green Party finally contrived to get power

indicators.note: contrived means manipulated or engineered, so these letters are rearranged
finally points to the closing letter of the word beside it

explanation.surface: The Green Party schemed its way into government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges GREEN into ENERG; Y is the last letter of 'Party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: energy is power or force, as in electrical power supply.

clue.text: Feelings shown by people put into some distress

indicators.note: to distress is to batter or age artificially, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People in trouble show what they feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' joins: the words 'into' and 'some' are put in distress, their eight letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: emotions are the feelings people display, such as joy or grief.

clue.text: Honoured with high rank in the finish

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

parts.note: an end is a finish
noble means of high rank, aristocratic

explanation.surface: Someone finally given a title at the end of their career.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be raised to the nobility, a high honour.

clue.text: Smile upon frolic that's spontaneous

indicators.note: to frolic is to romp about playfully, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A smile, a romp, and it's all unplanned.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: acting on impulse means doing it spontaneously, without forethought.

clue.text: It sounds a beastly form of warfare

indicators.note: the clue says the word is heard rather than read, so a like-sounding word is entered

parts.note: a beast such as the great ape of African forests

explanation.surface: A remark that some kind of fighting has an animal name.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerilla warfare is irregular fighting by small independent bands, so the word describes a form of war.

clue.text: Bob indicates a more direct route

definitions.meaning: a bob is a short haircut
a quicker way than the usual road

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob points out a quicker way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the hairstyle. 'indicates' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a short cut of hair such as a bob, and a quicker path.

clue.text: When children are about the dog is tied up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in biblical usage
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: The dog is kept on a lead whenever children are around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: secured means fastened or tied firmly.

clue.text: Close to anger

definitions.meaning: to bring to an end, as with winding up a company or meeting
to tease or provoke someone deliberately

explanation.surface: Someone is on the verge of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: bring to a conclusion, and needle someone until they are irritated.

clue.text: Read by custom on the first of December

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
use means custom or habit

indicators.note: the first of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Something read according to tradition on the first day of December.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perused means read through carefully.

clue.text: Fast sailing ships take the wool crops

definitions.meaning: sleek nineteenth-century merchant sailing vessels built for speed
shears used to crop a sheep's fleece

explanation.surface: Ships carry away the season's wool harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: speedy tea ships of the 1800s, and shears or hair trimmers that clip.

clue.text: Kind of toaster gets dad out of bed

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: A father is roused by his toast springing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up toaster ejects the bread when done, so the term names a kind of toaster.

clue.text: A new paper to be published

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A fresh newspaper is due to go to press.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a book or article is said to appear when it is published.

clue.text: Strange direction leading to lake

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so this piece sits in front of the next

parts.note: E is east, a compass direction
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Odd instructions guiding someone towards a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: eerie means strange and unsettling, weird.

clue.text: Speed of a ship steaming to tie up

definitions.meaning: a unit of nautical speed, one nautical mile per hour
to fasten a rope or string with a twist

explanation.surface: A steamship slows to moor at the quay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steaming' only joins the two definitions, adding to the nautical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the nautical unit of speed, and to fasten rope in a loop.

clue.text: Hastily made and hoisted a flag

explanation.surface: A banner quickly stitched and then raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to run up clothes is to sew them fast, and to run up a flag is to raise it.

clue.text: Ground and house might be theirs

definitions.text: Ground and house might be theirs

parts.words: Ground and house might be theirs
parts.note: reads as property owners owning land and a home, but also hints at ground (land) and the House of Lords (lords)

explanation.surface: Property owners might possess both land and building.
explanation.definitionFit: People who own property and let it to tenants own the ground and buildings.

clue.text: Deathly pale, going out to appear as Hamlet?

indicators.note: going out suggests leaving the ordered state, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor looks ghastly white on the way to the stage as the Danish prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the title role, Hamlet, is to act the principal part; the question mark marks it as an example.
